info.summary: Open data on tracked off-plan property projects (anonymous), public log proofs, market statistics and the partner risk feed.
info.description: Read-only HTTP API of kolaboro.com. Projects are anonymous until verification is complete and the developer has had 10 working days to reply. Scores describe what is public about a project, not whether it is genuine. Open endpoints need no key and are cached at the edge (usually 10 minutes). Answers of /api/open/* and the partner feed are signed: x-kolaboro-signature is base64 Ed25519 over "kolaboro-sig-v1\n" + SHA-256 hex of the body, key id in x-kolaboro-key-id, public keys at https://kolaboro.com/.well-known/kolaboro-keys.json. Response schemas in this file were inferred from live responses on the date in x-kolaboro-checked and are checked against the live API every day by the Kolaboro data catalog job (results: https://kolaboro.com/data/#contracts). They describe what the API returned, which can grow over time.

get.description: Model card and summary of the risk-pattern model (from /data/risk.json). It ranks; it does not predict.

model_card.name: Kolaboro risk patterns
model_card.purpose: Show which tracked projects look unusual on public warning signs compared with all other tracked projects, and why. It ranks; it does not predict.
model_card.not_for: It is not a fraud predictor and not a verdict. No project in our data has a confirmed outcome (fraud, collapse or delivery), so nothing could be trained or tested against outcomes.

features_not_available.why: The front-loaded feature uses only advertised plans that state a clear share due on completion (175 projects). Plans written as ranges, dated schedules or options are left out rather than guessed.
Advertised price per m2 versus official sales in the same area exists for 21 Dubai projects only (see /prices/). Too sparse across all markets to be a fair feature yet.

method: Each feature is turned into a robust z-score against all 896 tracked projects. Yes/no signs: (1 - p) / sqrt(p (1 - p)) when present, where p is the share of projects showing it, so a rare sign weighs more than a common one. Numbers: (x - median) / (1.4826 x MAD). Numbers that most projects do not ha...

The score is the sum of these z-scores, so every point of it is traceable to one feature. Projects at or above the 95th percentile of the score are labelled "unusual", at or above the 75th "somewhat unusual".
limits: Features come from what developers publish and what we could check; a project that publishes less can look calmer than it is.
Common signs (no deposit protection stated, no permit claimed) weigh little because most projects show them; that is a property of the peer group, not a judgement that they are safe.

get.description: Which official registers can be checked automatically (from /data/register-checks.json).

method: Every register linked on /registers/ was requested once by our checker (user agent KolaboroRegisterCheck/1.0), after reading the site's robots.txt. We store the time, HTTP status, content type, size and SHA-256 of the exact bytes received.

A register counts as automated only when a lookup by number works over plain HTTP, without a login, captcha or JavaScript, and robots.txt does not forbid it. Everything else is listed as browser only or manual, which is the honest state today.

get.description: Questionnaire, measurement and status of the mystery shopper programme.

why_not_started: Kolaboro has no mailbox for sending research enquiries yet, and the site's code has no path for sending email to developers.
The owner has not yet approved the wording of the enquiry below.
example.sender_policy: Enquiries will come from a Kolaboro research mailbox and will not pretend to be a named private buyer. They ask exactly what a careful buyer would ask. Replies are stored privately; only aggregate numbers per market and per anonymous project id are published.

questionnaire.question: What is the building permit number for this project, which authority issued it, and on what date?
questionnaire.checkable_answer: A permit or project number we can look up on the official register for the market (for example PBG in Indonesia, the DLD project number or Trakheesi permit in Dubai, a planning reference in the UK).

questionnaire.question: Who holds the land title for the plot, what type of title is it, and what is the certificate number? If the units are leasehold, is the lease registered, and what are its start date and term?
questionnaire.checkable_answer: The title holder's legal name and title type and number, matching the seller on the draft contract.

measurement.definition: Share of enquiries that receive any reply from the developer or its sales agent within 14 days. One reminder is sent after 7 days.
Hours from our enquiry to the first reply, reported as the median and the 90th percentile, per market.

example.publication: Per market: number of enquiries, response rate, median and 90th percentile time to first answer, share of checkable answers per question, number of contradictions. Per anonymous project id: replied or not, time to answer, questions answered with something checkable, contradictions. No names of devel...
example.plan: First wave: 30 projects across 3 markets with the most tracked projects (Dubai, Bali, Phuket), chosen at random by a published seed, then repeated every quarter.
needed_to_start: A sending mailbox on a Kolaboro domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up, for example research@kolaboro.com through an email provider (the owner creates the account).
The owner's written approval of the enquiry wording above and of the sender policy.

get.description: Summary of /data/visual-diff.json: method, limits, totals, recent changes. Geometry only, no images.

example.what: Where the pages of tracked developer websites visibly changed, as page geometry only. No screenshots are published: they would copy the developers' own copyrighted images. Before, after and highlighted diff images are kept privately for 90 days and are available to a buyer on request.
example.trigger: A capture is taken when the research agent sees the page text change (text fingerprint), or once to make a first baseline.
method: Full-page screenshot in Chromium at 1280 px wide, animations off, lazy images scrolled into view, capped at 8000 px of page height.
Both captures scaled to 560 px wide and turned grey. Pixel rows are aligned between the two captures (longest matching blocks), so content that only moved down is not counted as changed.
caveats: Carousels, rotating banners, cookie notices, text that animates in and personalised content can still show as changes. In a test of 16 sites captured twice a few minutes apart with no real change, 2 crossed the 1 % threshold. A listed change is a prompt to look, confirmed by eye on the private image...
The first capture of a project is only a baseline: a change can be shown only from the second capture on.
